title: 08 Rational expressions and equations: Visual Guide
outline: Title: 08 Rational expressions and equations: Visual Guide

1. Factor Then Cancel | (x^2 - a^2)/(x^2 - a x) factored and reduced live from a slider on a, beside the factoring and domain rules it is built from, with a value table comparing the original and the simplified form and a button that performs the illegal term cancellation | canceling is division, so only a shared FACTOR may go, and the restrictions x != 0 and x != a come from the original denominator and survive the cancellation as a hole

2. Multiply And Divide | a multiply/divide switch over (kx/3)×(9/x^2) and (x^2-1)/(x+b) ÷ (x-1)/(x+b), each cancelled step by step and verified numerically at a draggable test point | multiply straight across after cancelling across both fractions, divide by multiplying by the reciprocal, and remember that dividing adds the restriction that the divisor's numerator is nonzero

3. Common Denominator | two rational terms with draggable numerators and denominators, combined over the LCD, with the naive add-the-tops-add-the-bottoms answer evaluated alongside the true value at a test point | like denominators combine numerators only, unlike denominators must first be rescaled by a disguised 1, and 1/(x+1) + 1/(x-1) is 2x/(x^2-1) rather than 2/(2x)

4. Clear The Denominators | n/(x+c) = r solved by clearing the LCD with live steps and an accept/reject check, plus a second shape 1/(x-1) + 1/(x+1) = k/(x^2-1) whose answer x = k/2 crosses the forbidden values as k is dragged | multiplying by the LCD is an equivalence only away from the excluded values, so every candidate must be tested against the original denominators and a rejected candidate means no solution

5. Miles Per Hour | distance and time sliders driving 120/r = 3 against three distractor equations scored numerically and by units, plus a combined-work widget solving 1/a + 1/b = 1/T | an unknown rate lands in a denominator, the units test picks the model where the arithmetic cannot, and a model carries physical restrictions on top of the algebraic ones
